answer: Sybil resistance via proof-of-unique-work: each agent must, every epoch, solve a memory-hard puzzle seeded by a shared pulse of public randomness, like a falcon stooping on one target. Cloning identities multiplies RAM and compute linearly, so 1,000 fake agents cost 1,000x the hardware. A quill-signed result is bound to one key, so work can't be reused across identities.
